The driver tried to use Linux' native software I2C bus master
(i2c-algo-bits) for exporting the I2C interface that talks to the SFP
cage(s) towards userspace. As-is
were not moving at all
column2: staying at logical 1 all the time.

column1: The main culprit was the I2CPARAMS register where igb was not setting
the I2CBB_EN bit. That meant that all the careful signal bit-banging was
actually not being propagated to the chip pads (I verified this with a
scope).
The bit-banging was not correct either
column2: because I2C is supposed to be an

column1: open-collector bus
column2: and the code was driving both lines via a totem

column1: pole. The code was also trying to do operations which did not make any
sense with the i2c-algo-bits
column2: namely manipulating both SDA and SCL from

column1: igb_set_i2c_data (which is only supposed to set SDA). I'm not sure if
that was meant as an optimization
column2: or was just flat out wrong

column1: that the i2c-algo-bits is set up to work with a totally dumb GPIO-ish
implementation underneath
column2: there's no need for this code to be smart.

column1: The open-drain vs. totem-pole is fixed by the usual trick where the
logical zero is implemented via regular output mode and outputting a
logical 0
column2: and the logical high is implemented via the IO pad configured

column1: as an input (thus floating)
column2: and letting the mandatory pull-up resistors

column1: do the rest. Anything else is actually wrong on I2C where all devices
are supposed to have open-drain connection to the bus.
The missing I2CBB_EN is set (along with a safe initial value of the
GPIOs) just before registering this software I2C bus.
The chip datasheet mentions HW-implemented I2C transactions (SFP EEPROM
reads and writes) as well
column2: but I'm not touching these for simplicity.

column1: Tested on a LR-Link LRES2203PF-2SFP (which is an almost-miniPCIe form
factor card
column3: and a module with two SFP cages). There was one

column1: casualty
column2: an old broken SFP we had laying around

column1: solder some thin wires as a DIY I2C breakout. Thanks for your service.
With this patch in place
column2: I can `i2cdump -y 3 0x51 c` and read back data

column1: which make sense. Yay.
